description: Inputs passed to the Accountable DVN attestation policy WASM at evaluation time. Shape confirmed 2026-08-13 against a live Accountable node (axis.accountable.capital:8443/dashboard) — see README 'Verified against a live node'.

nodeUrl.description: Base URL of the specific attested entity's Accountable node (e.g. 'https://axis.accountable.capital:8443'). Accountable runs one self-hosted node per attested entity, not one shared multi-tenant API — this identifies which entity's book is being evaluated.

dataSource.description: Key into that node's dataSources map (e.g. 'Blockchain', or an exchange/custodian source name) — which of the entity's connected sources this evaluation gates on.

rpcUrl.description: Ethereum-compatible JSON-RPC endpoint used to read the on-chain price the attested value is compared against.

onchainPrice.description: On-chain price source the mandate author trusts as authoritative for this entity's token (e.g. an ERC-4626 share-price accessor). Caller-supplied, not a pack default — which price counts as authoritative is a mandate-author decision.

decimals.description: Decimals to scale the raw eth_call return by. Defaults to 18 when omitted.

prevSnapshot.description: Optional prior evaluation's snapshot_last_updated_ms for this exact (nodeUrl, dataSource) pair. No 'carry-forward' field exists on Accountable's node API, so this pack detects a reused (non-fresh) reading by diffing lastUpdated against the previous check, the same way the redstone pack detects sustained divergence. Omit or set to null on the first-ever evaluation.

lastUpdatedMs.description: The dataSource's lastUpdated value (ms epoch) recorded at the previous evaluation.

roster.description: Whether this entity/node is on the mandate author's covered-entity roster. A single Accountable node has no visibility into which other entities the DVN covers, so this is a caller-supplied fact (from whatever layer aggregates across nodes), not something this oracle fetches.

networkStatus.description: Network-wide success/total counts for the circuit-breaker check. Same reasoning as roster: a single node cannot report on the health of the network as a whole, so this is caller-supplied.
